Senses.Explanation: Literally, the king (王) of geese (鵝). In the Chan corpus this bird is overwhelmingly the goose king that selects milk from water. One instruction gives the image directly: 'there is milk in water; people do not see it; the goose king selects it.' Another says that when water and milk are mixed, the goose king eats the milk. Masters then use the fixed line 'the goose king selects the milk, naturally not of the duck kind' as an appraisal after cases and answers. In a hall exchange a monk asks the purport of that line and the master answers, 'south of the river there is; north of the river there is not,' without explaining the bird further. Another address pairs capacities: it takes a goose king to select milk and a lion to bite. A verse also reverses the stock contrast: under one strike, 'the goose king becomes a duck; the soft-shelled turtle becomes a tortoise.' The Zen deviation is this legendary bird's repeated use—and deliberate reversal—as a teaching-seat appraisal of selection and discrimination; the entry does not add a hidden object beyond the milk, water, goose, and duck named by the records.
Senses.Note: Exact count: 129 hits in 79 allowlisted texts. The goose-king-selects-milk formula (鵝王擇乳) has 69 hits in 48 texts; not-of-the-duck-kind (素非鴨類) has 55 in 36. One legendary-bird sense. Family checked against selecting milk (擇乳), water and milk (水乳), duck kind (鴨類), choosing the teaching (擇法), and possessing the eye (具眼).
